batch_invariance_check.window: last 200 households of batch 1 and first 200 of batch 2, re-materialized together in one child

poverty_spm_check.rule: exclude any compiled target whose name, or whose base/source/filter variable, contains 'poverty' or 'spm'

employment_income.household_value: household value of the target's measure

agi_or_total_income.household_value: household value of the target's measure

frozen_draw.route_to_ids: scenarios.csv scenario_json.metadata.household_id (PolicyBench writes the source household id there)
frozen_draw.reproduction: policybench/scenarios.py draw re-run here: eligibility filter, numpy.random.default_rng(seed).choice(ids, requested, replace=False, p=w/sum(w)), then split_scenarios' sha256 id-hash public split

pps_first_order_inclusion.weight_used: sum of eligible design weights / 100 (self-weighting approximation)
pps_first_order_inclusion.note: microcosm.calibrate.exact_k supplies inclusion probabilities only for its own Sampford draw (select_exact_k); it has no function for numpy Generator.choice(replace=False, p=...), so the self-weighting approximation is used and checked empirically against the seed draws (sampling_distribution.json self_weighting_check)
